Article Title: SC to UP police: Educate officers on investigation
Article Text:
Supreme Court slams UP police for "slipshod investigation", orders Rs 6 lakh compensation for man held six years without evidence.

Appalled at the way UP cops carried out probe: SC

NEW DELHI: In a severe indictment of Uttar Pradesh police for carrying out a “slipshod investigation” that resulted in a man being in custody for six years when there was no evidence against him, Supreme Court Monday said the state cannot shirk its responsibility to protect citizens and directed it to pay a compensation of Rs 6 lakh to him.“This is a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with, resulting in the prosecution putting into jeopardy a person’s life and liberty,” SC noted at the outset of its verdict.On Sept 30, in a separate matter, the top court had slammed UP police for not naming the accused in a road accident case.It would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI if the state police works with an agenda and does cover-up jobs, court had said, noting the accused had not been named despite the complainant catching him on the spot and handing him over to police.In the present case, a bench of J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there was no evidence to implicate the person in a kidnapping and murder case. It noted he was never named in the FIR and police made him an accused on the basis that he was seen in CCTV footage. SC said it was “appalled at the manner in which investigation was carried out”. “It is unfortunate that despite no evidence against the petitioner, he was imprisoned for six years as an undertrial.Based on a slipshod investigation, a haphazard prosecution was carried out, which resulted, fortunately, in the acquittal of the accused. We cannot but deprecate the manner in which the probe was carried out and prosecution conducted,” SC said. “State police would do well to educate their officers in the process of investigation.”Making the state accountable for police’s misdeed, the court said six years have been erased from the man’s life on the strength of a concocted story built on mere surmises and conjectures, and the state has to pay compensation.“The state cannot shirk from its responsibility to protect its citizens, especially when a person arraigned in a criminal case is presumed innocent until proven guilty. The investigation and prosecuting agencies exist not merely to, and by whatever means, bring in a conviction. They should recognise themselves to be essential stakeholders in the justice delivery system, ensuring justice, not only to the victim, the de facto complainant and the injured but also to the accused,” the SC bench said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court slams UP police for "slipshod investigation", orders Rs 6 lakh compensation for man held six years without evidence. SC said it was “appalled at the manner in which investigation was carried out” “It is unfortunate that despite no evidence against the petitioner, he was imprisoned for six years as an undertrial,” SC said.

Article Title: 'Not concerned with any individual': Congress urges SC to summon records on SIR after EC's affidavit
Article Text:

The Indian Express

NEW DELHI: Congress on Monday urged the Supreme Court to summon all relevant records related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, following the Election Commission's affidavit stating that all decisions were taken unanimously.Congress MP Imran Masood said the issue was about adherence to the rules and that the questions concerned the deletion of votes and Form 6."The Supreme Court should summon all the relevant records; even if all three agreed, the core issue remains 'Form 6'. If all three made an incorrect decision, then it is still wrong, isn't it? The issue is about adherence to the rules. We are not concerned with any individual," Masood said."The question concerns 'Form 6'. The question concerns the deletion of votes. How could the issue be resolved? The Election Commissioner is not the issue here. The issue is the theft of votes," he added.This comes hours after the poll panel submitted a counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court, defending its functioning and the conduct of the SIR exercise.The poll body rejected allegations of irregularities and questioned the basis of a petition challenging its decision-making process.The Election Commission stated this in its response to pleas alleging that it took several decisions without the approval of the two election commissioners, including "changes" in Form 6.The law and the prescribed Form 6 for voter registration were not amended, the poll panel said in its counter-affidavit filed in the Supreme Court with the unanimous approval of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the two election commissioners.The EC said the SIR orders issued on June 24, 2025, October 27, 2025, and May 14, 2026, were approved unanimously by the commission's three members - the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two election commissioners.It said the CEC could not be restrained from functioning, as newspaper reports were not considered evidence in the eyes of the law.Earlier, on October 5, the top court said it would examine all decisions of the EC and annul those found not to be in accordance with the law, as it issued notices to the Centre and the poll body.The pleas were filed afterreported on September 25 that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the previous 10 months to decisions and orders on the SIR of electoral rolls that they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. The claim has sparked protests by opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which have demanded the removal of CEC Kumar.
Article Summary: Congress MP Imran Masood said the issue was about adherence to the rules. This comes hours after the poll panel submitted a counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court. The poll body rejected allegations of irregularities and questioned the basis of a petition challenging its decision-making process.

NEW DELHI: Democratic Trinamool Congress chief Ritabrata Banerjee on Monday accused the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction of attempting to loot a truck carrying its affidavits to the Election Commission in New Delhi.In a social media post on X, Ritabrata said his faction had dispatched documents by road on October 24 to meet the deadline for submitting evidence to the poll panel. He alleged that unidentified miscreants tried to take control of the truck and snatch the documents near the Haryana border in the early hours of Monday, but workers accompanying the consignment resisted the attempt."Chartered Flight has carried Kalighat's affidavits to Delhi on October 25 evening. Our affidavits are being transported to Delhi by road. Our workers have started with our documents on October 24 morning for depositing in ECI," Ritabrata said."Half an hour ago there were attempts to take control of the truck and snatch our documents. Our workers have resisted bravely. The fight is on. A fight between Chartered Culture versus Grass Root resolve. Despots will not succeed in their attempt at organised loot in every sphere," he added.Meanwhile, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's Rajya Sabha member Dola Sen dismissed the allegation and asserted that people were the ultimate judge.Lok Sabha MP Kalyan Banerjee also questioned the route the vehicle had allegedly taken."The Ritabrata-led outfit enjoys protection of the central police force. How can the truck be seized when it is protected by the CRPF jawans? Also, why would a truck travelling from Kolkata to Delhi take a Haryana detour?"These are all drama hatched by the faction which enjoys the support of the BJP top brass. Their allegation is utterly baseless," he said.This comes amid an ongoing battle between the rival factions of the party, which split after the 2026 West Bengal assembly elections. NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra government on Monday constituted a three-member special investigation team (SIT) to conduct an in-depth inquiry into an audio clip released by Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange.As per the official order, the SIT will comprise Shailesh Balkawade, additional commissioner, south region, Mumbai, who will head it; Vijaykant Sagar, deputy commissioner of police (South Zone 3, Mumbai); and Bajrang Bansode, deputy commissioner of police (Cyber, Crime Branch, Mumbai)."The SIT will undertake a forensic examination, technical analysis, and comprehensive, impartial investigation into the recording. Article Title: Broke locks, scaled walls: Congress MPs named in Jamia FIR amid students' unrest
Article Text:
The FIR also alleges that people who were neither students nor university employees entered the campus, defaced walls with objectionable graffiti, damaged property and manhandled university employees, leaving some injured.

NEW DELHI: Breaking a university gate lock, scaling a boundary wall and allegedly damaging campus property. These are among the incidents cited in an FIR against the Congress MPs following the students' protest at Jamia Millia Islamia.The complaint, filed by registrar Md Mahtab Alam Rizvi, alleges that Congress MPs Imran Pratapgarhi and Imran Masood entered the campus without authorisation on separate occasions as the agitation for the restoration of the students' union intensified.The FIR, registered at Jamia Nagar police station on Sunday, details a series of incidents between October 21 and 24. Pratapgarhi allegedly broke the lock of gate number 4A to enter the campus on October 21. Two days later, Masood allegedly climbed a boundary wall near Gafoor Nagar with the help of a ladder to gain entry.The complaint also flags an incident on October 24, when outsiders allegedly occupied and locked the department of political science building, disrupting academic activities. It further alleges that people who were neither students nor university employees entered the campus, defaced walls with objectionable graffiti, damaged property and manhandled university employees, leaving some injured.The allegations extend beyond the two Congress MPs.The registrar's complaint mentions Samajwadi Party MP Mohibbullah Nadvi, who was detained while on his way to the campus, as well as other political leaders who allegedly visited the protest site without prior intimation to the university administration.The FIR invokes provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to criminal trespass, wrongful restraint, voluntarily causing hurt, mischief, criminal intimidation, criminal conspiracy and common intention.It also cites the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act, 1984, and the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2007.The campus has been witnessing protests since October 12, with students demanding the restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students' Union (JMISU), whose elections have not been held since 2006. Protesters are also seeking the withdrawal of disciplinary action against students involved in the agitation.As tensions mounted, the university moved classes across all courses online, citing concerns over students' safety and security. It has maintained that Gate No. 18 is the designated location for protests and described the gathering at the Gulistan-e-Ghalib lawns as an unauthorised occupation.The Students' Federation of India (SFI), Jamia unit, has, meanwhile, alleged that police detained students outside Gate No. 7 and that university officials tried to forcibly remove protesters, dismantle their tents and drag women students during a confrontation. These allegations could not be independently verified.
Article Summary: FIR alleges Congress MPs Imran Pratapgarhi and Imran Masood entered campus without authorisation. It also alleges that people who were neither students nor university employees entered the campus, defaced walls with objectionable graffiti, damaged property and manhandled university employees.

Article Title: Congress to hold ‘Vote Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1; Amit Shah to lead padayatra in T'gana on Nov 2
Article Text:
Congress will hold ‘vote bachao, desh bachao’ rally on Nov 1 in Delhi, while Amit Shah will attend the ‘loktantra bachao, arajakta hatao’ padayatra on Nov 2 in Telangana

NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold amega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on November 1, party president Mallikarjun Kharge said on Monday. The protest comes over the alleged vote theft, demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an immediate halt of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah is also set to attend a BJP foot march in Telangana a day later, on November 2, to counter what the party calls the Congress's “false narrative” against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao announced Shah's participation in the November 2padayatra on Monday.The announcement comes amid a political row over the SIR exercise, with the Congress accusing the Election Commission of large-scale electoral irregularities.“They (Congress) are trying to create anarchy in the state and country. That's why we are going to organise a padayatra with the theme. Amit Shah ji will attend the padayatra on 2nd (of November),” news agency PTI reported, quoting Rao.Kharge announced the November 1 rally in a video shared on X, alleging that the constitutional right to vote of millions of Indians was under threat.“The constitutional right of the Indian people to cast their votes is under threat. CEC Gyanesh Kumar is solely responsible for this; he has acted entirely at the behest of the Prime Minister and the Home Minister,” Kharge said.Kharge also criticised the government over inflation.In his video address, he said, “Greetings, friends. It is the festive season, yet you are currently grappling with back-breaking inflation. The government, however, is completely unconcerned—all they know how to do is steal votes. Large-scale vote theft has taken place, and it continues even now.”Announcing the rally, he said, “In this regard, a 'Save the Vote, Save the Nation' (Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao) mega-rally will be held on November 1st at the historic Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.”“I appeal to you to participate actively in this rally to protect our Constitution and democracy, and to help make this campaign a success. Long live the Constitution! Jai Hind!” he added.Rao accused the Congress of spreading misinformation about the electoral roll revision and challenged Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy to identify voters whose names had been wrongly deleted.Observing that Congress was spreading lies over the SIR exercise, Rao said he was ready to visit the chief minister's native village, Kondareddypalle, to check how many voters' names had been removed from the rolls.He said genuine voters whose names were deleted had the option of getting them included again. Rao also asked Congress ministers in Telangana to identify at least 10 voters whose names had been deleted and explain the reasons for their removal.Responding to allegations that 13 crore voters had been removed during the SIR exercise, Rao claimed that they fell into the categories of 'Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate' (ASDD).Of these, he claimed, 2.8 crore were dead, three crore were absent or untraceable when booth-level officers visited them, 6.3 crore had permanently shifted and nearly one crore names were registered at multiple locations. He cited the example of a man in Hyderabad who had admitted to having voter registrations at three places.Rao also criticised Kharge over his remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, alleging that Congress was unable to accept that a 'chaiwala' had become the country's Prime Minister. He said the party was desperate to return to power after losing elections since 2014.The Telangana BJP president asked party workers to burn Congress effigies at district headquarters on Monday in protest against Kharge's remarks.He also took exception to Congress leaders from Telangana travelling to Delhi for the November 1 rally, citing water shortages in the state. Rao claimed that more than 300 of Telangana's over 600 mandals were facing drought-like conditions due to a rainfall deficit.Pointing to the impact of El Nino on water availability in Hyderabad, he said around 8,000 water tankers were being booked daily in the city. He urged Revanth Reddy to focus on addressing the water crisis instead.On the chief minister's recent pitch for Rahul Gandhi to become Prime Minister, Rao said the BJP's graph had risen since Gandhi began occupying leadership positions in the Congress.Taking a swipe at the Congress leader, Rao said, "you cannot market a failed product".
Article Summary: Congress to hold 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao' rally on Nov 1 in Delhi. Amit Shah to attend 'loktantra bachao, arajakta hatao' padayatra on Nov 2 in Telangana. Announcement comes amid a political row over the SIR exercise.

NEW DELHI: BJP workers on Monday staged protests in Bihar, Jammu and Bengaluru against Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's controversial 'baap' remark against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, demanding an apology from the Congress chief.The protests came a day after Kharge, speaking at an event in Patna, responded to a person from the audience who said that PM Modi would not go anywhere. "Modi ka baap bhi jayega (Even Modi's father will have to go)," Kharge said, triggering criticism from BJP leaders.The remark was made during a programme marking the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar's first chief minister, Shrikrishna Singh.Delhi BJP workers and leaders staged a protest near Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence on Rajaji Marg on Monday over his alleged disparaging remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The protest turned tense as demonstrators attempted to break through police barricades and march towards Kharge's residence.Police stopped the protesters as they tried to march from Sena Bhawan circle towards the Congress president's residence. Around 2,000 BJP workers and leaders, including Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra, were detained, the Delhi BJP said in a statement.Amid heavy police deployment in the Sena Bhawan area, the detained BJP workers and leaders were packed into buses and taken to Mandir Marg police station.They were later released, according to the party's statement.The BJP had called for nationwide protests over Kharge's remarks at an event in Patna, escalating its confrontation with the Congress over the alleged comments against the prime minister.In Bengaluru, BJP leaders and workers staged a demonstration at Freedom Park, demanding an unconditional apology from Kharge over his remarks.Police detained several BJP leaders, including Karnataka assembly leader of opposition R Ashoka and former minister CN Ashwath Narayan, during the protest.BJP leaders accused the Congress president of making offensive remarks against the Prime Minister and his family.In Patna, BJP workers took out a 'Jan Akrosh March' under the leadership of Bihar BJP president Sanjay Saraogi.The protesters marched from the party headquarters towards Income Tax Golambar, raising slogans against Kharge and the Congress. They also burnt an effigy of the Congress president."Yesterday, all limits were crossed when the platform to celebrate the birth anniversary of Shrikrishna Singh, the architect of modern Bihar, was used to make abusive remarks about the late father of the Prime Minister," Saraogi said.He accused the Congress of making personal attacks against Modi out of political frustration and demanded an apology from Kharge and Rahul Gandhi."The Congress, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi must apologise to the people of the country," he said.In Jammu, BJP leaders and workers staged a protest at Dogra Chowk, raising slogans against Kharge and the Congress. Led by BJP MLA Shagun Parihar and Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha's Jammu and Kashmir president Arun Prabhat, the protesters marched through Dogra Chowk, burnt posters of Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, and staged a brief sit-in on the road.Parihar condemned the remarks, saying they were disrespectful not only to the Prime Minister's late father but also to elderly people who had passed away."If they do not respect the prime minister's father, how will they respect the father of an ordinary citizen?" she asked. Protests were also reported from Samba, Kathua, Poonch, Udhampur, Rajouri, Doda, Kishtwar and Reasi districts. Similar demonstrations were held in Delhi and Lucknow as part of the BJP's nationwide protest against Kharge's remarks.Meanwhile, the Congress defended its president, claiming that a BJP supporter had first insulted Kharge's father during the Patna event. Congress leader Pawan Khera said Kharge was referring to the RSS as PM Modi's "ideological father", rather than his biological father. RJD leader Bhai Virendra also defended Kharge, describing his remarks as a "slip of the tongue" and saying he did not need to apologise.However, RJD MP Manoj Jha said such conduct was not expected from a senior leader like Kharge, while questioning what he described as selective outrage over remarks made by political leaders. Union home minister Amit Shah also criticised Kharge, accusing the Congress of repeatedly crossing the limits of political decorum by targeting PM Modi and his family.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Monday slammed Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over his controversial remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s late father, saying the statement had left him shocked and hurt. He also criticised the Congress for defending Kharge’s comments instead of expressing regret over the controversy.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's 'baap' remark against Prime Minister Narendra Modi triggers nationwide protests. BJP workers stage protests in Bihar, Jammu and Bengaluru against Congress president. Congress defends its president's remarks, claiming he was insulted by a BJP supporter.

Article Summary: AISA national president Neha Bora claims that protesting journalists have been detained at the Delhi Cantonment Police Station. Congress' Patna teachers constituency candidate Sanjay Yadav held a protest outside the counting centre at Bankipur school, alleging malpractices and the "absence of CCTV cameras" in the counting hall."Electoral malpractices have been reported. CCTV cameras have been installed outside the counting hall, but no device was placed inside the hall. It is an attempt to orchestrate malpractices," Yadav told news agency PTI.A commotion broke out at the Bankipur vote-counting centre in Patna after a government employee was spotted carrying a bundle of files into the counting hall.Counting was underway for the Patna Graduates’ and Patna Teachers’ constituencies of the Bihar Legislative Council.Reporters and supporters of candidates surrounded the employee as he made his way to the venue, questioning why the files were being taken into the counting hall.Police personnel deployed outside the counting centre intervened and asked the employee to place the bundle on the ground.Counting is underway for five Maharashtra Legislative Council constituencies on Tuesday, with the results expected to test the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance’s handling of internal dissent and the Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi’s (MVA) efforts to capitalise on differences within the ruling coalition.A total of 182 candidates are contesting across three graduates’ and two teachers’ constituencies, which together have 10,68,072 registered voters. Polling was held on October 23 across 2,419 polling stations, recording an overall turnout of around 72.96%.The contests have drawn attention amid rebel candidates, competing alliance interests and differences within both camps. The results will determine representatives for the five constituencies and offer an indication of the parties’ support among graduates and teachers.Counting is underway for 19 Legislative Council (MLC) seats across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, with graduate and teacher constituencies in focus.In Bihar, the contest covers eight seats — four graduate constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi, and four teacher constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran. The terms of eight sitting MLCs are due to end on November 16.The elections are being closely watched as a political test for the Congress government, with both the ruling party and the BJP-JD(S) alliance seeking to demonstrate their organisational strength among graduates and teachers. The results will also indicate how effectively the BJP and JD(S) have managed to transfer votes to each other's candidates under their alliance.Four-tier security arrangements have been put in place. Police personnel have been deployed in two shifts of 12 hours each for counting-related duties, with around 400 personnel assigned to each shift. In addition, an external drone team, mounted police and mobile squads have also been deployed as part of the security arrangements. Everyone is expected to ensure that the entire process is conducted in accordance with the Election Commission's guidelines. If police assistance is required at any point, the authorities should be informed immediately: SSP KaustubhVote counting for 28 Legislative Council seats across Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra and Karnataka began on Tuesday. Polling for the seats was held on October 23.Security was tightened around the counting centre in Gorakhpur, with multiple layers of barricading and police personnel deployed to maintain order.In Uttar Pradesh, polling was held for 11 constituencies, including five Graduates' constituencies — Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut and Allahabad-Jhansi — and six Teachers' constituencies — Lucknow, Varanasi, Agra, Meerut, Bareilly-Moradabad and Gorakhpur-Faizabad.In Maharashtra, 182 candidates are contesting five seats. The election covers three Graduates' constituencies — Pune, Nagpur and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar — and two Teachers' constituencies in Pune and Amravati.Karnataka is witnessing elections to four Legislative Council seats, covering 17 districts across the state. The key constituencies include Bengaluru and North-East Teachers' constituencies, along with the West and South-East Graduates' constituencies.In Bihar, polling was held for eight seats — four Graduates' constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi, and four Teachers' constituencies in Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran.Counting began at 8am for the biennial elections to eight Bihar Legislative Council seats, with 90 candidates contesting four graduates’ constituencies and 60 in four teachers’ constituencies.Polling took place on October 23, recording a turnout of 82.85% in teachers’ constituencies and 53.42% in graduates’ seats. The four graduates’ constituencies — Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Kosi — had 4.92 lakh eligible voters, while the four teachers’ constituencies — Patna, Darbhanga, Tirhut and Saran — had 40,253 electors.Counting is being conducted at designated centres across the state. These include the Bankipur Government Girls’ Senior Secondary School in Patna, Khel Bhawan-cum-Vyayamshala Bhawan in Darbhanga, the MIT administrative block in Muzaffarpur for both Tirhut seats, and designated centres for the Kosi graduates’ and Saran teachers’ constituencies.The BJP has fielded candidates for four seats, while its ally JD(U) is contesting the remaining four. The Jan Suraaj Party, led by Prashant Kishor, is contesting all eight seats. The terms of the eight sitting MLCs expire on November 16.Counting also began at 8am for elections to five graduates’ and six teachers’ constituencies of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council.Chief electoral officer Navdeep Rinwa directed returning officers to ensure elaborate security arrangements and uninterrupted power supply at counting centres. Officials have been instructed to arrange automatic-switch generators, maintain CCTV surveillance and videography, restrict entry to authorised personnel and deploy trained counting staff.Additional personnel have been kept on reserve because Legislative Council elections use proportional representation through the single transferable vote system, which can make counting more time-consuming than conventional elections. Officials have also been directed to follow Election Commission guidelines and the Conduct of Elections Rules, with any negligence or procedural violations to be viewed seriously.In Maharashtra, counting began for five Legislative Council seats — three graduates’ and two teachers’ constituencies — involving 182 candidates. The constituencies had 10,68,072 registered voters and recorded an overall turnout of 72.96%.The contests are being closely watched for their implications for the BJP-led Mahayuti alliance and the opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), particularly amid rebel candidates and competing alliance interests.In Nagpur, BJP candidate Sudhakar Kohale is challenging sitting Congress MLC Abhijit Wanjarri. Pune graduates’ constituency has 47 candidates, including BJP nominee Smita Jadhav and NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar) candidate Harshada Deshmukh-Jadhav.In Pune teachers’ constituency, BJP nominee Kaustubh Gawde faces Congress MLC Jayant Asgaonkar, while Shiv Sena, led by Eknath Shinde, backs independent candidate Sachin Sanap. In Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, sitting MLC Satish Chavan faces NCP (SP) candidate Pratapsinh Patil, while Amravati teachers’ constituency features sitting MLC Kiran Sarnaik against Congress nominee Aditi Pohare and several rebel candidates.Amravati recorded the highest turnout at 92.6%, followed by Pune teachers’ at 85.86%, Nagpur graduates’ at 64.84%, Pune graduates’ at 62.76% and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar graduates’ at 59.12%.With preferential voting in place, the final outcome could depend on subsequent preferences if no candidate reaches the required quota on first preferences alone.Counting of votes for the Karnataka Legislative Council’s West Graduates’ Constituency began on Tuesday at the University of Agricultural Sciences in Dharwad. As the election follows the preferential voting system, counting is expected to continue for several rounds, with the final result likely to be declared late in the evening or around midnight.The constituency, which covers Dharwad, Haveri, Gadag and Uttara Kannada districts, recorded a voter turnout of 75.6% in the October 23 election. Of the 97,400 registered voters, 73,658 cast their votes.A candidate needs to secure 50% plus one of the valid votes to win in the first round. Fourteen candidates are in the fray, including BJP’s SV Sankanur, who won the seat in 2014 and 2020, Congress candidate Mohan Limbikai and independent candidate Kanthkumar.Regional commissioner and returning officer KM Janaki said on Monday that votes would be counted across 14 tables. The Election Commission has appointed additional assistant returning officers to ensure the smooth conduct of the process. The strongroom is scheduled to be opened at 7.55am.
Article Summary: Counting is underway for 19 Legislative Council (MLC) seats across Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, with graduate and teacher constituencies in focus. A commotion broke out at the Bankipur vote-counting centre in Patna after a government employee was spotted carrying a bundle of files into the counting hall. The elections are being closely watched as a political test for the Congress government.

Article Title: ‘Do you eat beef’: Coimbatore teacher under scanner after Dalit Class XI student dies by suicide
Article Text:
Peelamedu police have registered a case involving a teacher, headmaster, and two students related to a student’s suicide





COIMBATORE: Peelamedu police in the city have registered a case under three sections against four people, including two students of a government-aided school, in connection with the suicide of a Scheduled Caste student near Peelamedu.A. Akilan, 16, was a Class XI student of a government-aided school (KK Naidu) near Peelamedu. On Wednesday, his parents went to work while Akilan stayed at their home near Peelamedu.Upon returning from work, his mother, Kowsalya, found him hanging from the ceiling in a bedroom.She lodged a complaint with the Peelamedu police on Wednesday stating that Akilan had informed her that other students in the school were not talking to him after learning that he belonged to a Scheduled Caste.Furthermore, she alleged that the teacher had questioned the student about whether he ate beef, and the headmaster was accused of failing to take action regarding the incident.Peelamedu police have registered a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two fellow students in connection with Akilan's suicide, and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A. Akilan, 16, was a Class XI student of a government-aided school near Peelamedu. His mother, Kowsalya, found him hanging from the ceiling in a bedroom. Police have registered a case against the teacher, headmaster, and two fellow students.

Article Title: Delhi high court declines to halt probe against woman journalist accused of casteist remarks against ACP at Jantar Mantar, seeks police response
Article Text:
Delhi high court has issued a notice regarding an FIR against a woman journalist for alleged misconduct





NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Tuesday refused to stay the investigation into a case registered against a woman journalist over alleged casteist remarks and public humiliation of a police officer during a protest near Jantar Mantar earlier this month.Justice Mini Pushkarna clarified that the court was neither rejecting the interim prayer at this stage nor passing any order on it, news agency PTI reported.The court issued notice to the Delhi Police and the assistant commissioner of police (ACP), who filed the complaint, on the journalist’s plea seeking quashing of the FIR. It asked them to file their replies before November 16, the next date of hearing.“I am not rejecting any prayer as of now. I am only issuing notice to them. The matter needs consideration; list for final hearing on November 16,” the judge said.Earlier, the woman journalist had filed a sexual assault complaint against the official. The Delhi Police Crime Branch is investigating her complaint, PTI reported.The journalist’s counsel argued that the FIR lodged by the ACP was intended to intimidate her and prevent her from pursuing the complaint against him.The high court passed a similar order on a separate plea by a male colleague of the journalist, who has also sought quashing of the FIR registered against him.The Delhi Police registered the FIR against the independent journalist and others based on an official’s complaint, PTI reported.The officer, who is posted at the Connaught Place sub-division of New Delhi district, alleged that casteist remarks, public humiliation and defamation were directed at him during the protest.The FIR invokes relevant provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Sections 221 (obstructing a public servant from discharging duty), 356(2) (defamation) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi high court refuses to stay investigation into a case registered against a woman journalist over alleged casteist remarks and public humiliation of a police officer. The court issued notice to the Delhi Police and the assistant commissioner of police (ACP), who filed the complaint, on the journalist’s plea seeking quashing of the FIR.

Article Title: MCD JE suspended over demolition of Kanjhawala cow shelter
Article Text:
New Delhi:





A junior engineer at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has been suspended over the demolition of an upcoming cow shelter in Kanjhawala, chief minister Rekha Gupta said Monday. Disciplinary proceedings have also been initiated.The action comes a day after Gupta met animal welfare activist Jagriti Mishra and assured her of financial assistance of Rs 5 lakh for the damage caused to the proposed gaushala in Nijampur village in northwest Delhi.“Junior engineer of MCD in the case involving animal welfare activist Jagriti Mishra has been suspended, and disciplinary proceedings have been initiated,” the chief minister said.“Public office carries a responsibility to serve citizens with sensitivity and integrity. Our govt is committed to examining every complaint fairly and following due process. Any misconduct established through the proceedings will invite strict action,” she said.During Sunday’s meeting, Mishra told the chief minister that some local men claiming to be associated with the local councillor had threatened her against constructing the gaushala on the land in Nijampur village. She alleged that the upcoming cow shelter was subsequently demolished on the instructions of a junior engineer.Gupta had assured Mishra of all possible support and directed the district magistrate and deputy commissioner of police to extend assistance and ensure her protection from those involved in the alleged threats.
Article Summary: A junior engineer at the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has been suspended over the demolition of an upcoming cow shelter in Kanjhawala. Disciplinary proceedings have also been initiated. The action comes a day after Gupta met animal welfare activist Jagriti Mishra and assured her of financial assistance.

Article Title: ‘Why no arrests yet?’ Congress questions police over gang-rape allegations against ex-BJP MLA Narendra Pawar, cites inaction
Article Text:
Congress leader Kanchan Kulkarni has raised concerns about the police investigation and alleged inaction





KALYAN: More than a month after a 22-year-old married woman accused former BJP MLA Narendra Pawar and dismissed police constable Shailesh Patil of gang-raping her at a farmhouse in Bhiwandi taluka, the Congress has questioned the police investigation, alleging that the accused are being shielded.Kanchan Kulkarni, Congress group leader in the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation (KDMC) who had helped victim to get FIR registered in this case, has accused the police of inaction and questioned why the two accused have not been arrested despite the seriousness of the allegations.She alleged that the police were extending help to the accused and demanded accountability over the delay in their arrest.The case was registered at Padgha police station in September following a complaint by the woman, who alleged that Pawar had called her to his office on the pretext of helping resolve a dispute with her husband.According to the FIR, she was subsequently taken to a farmhouse in Bapgaon, where Pawar and Patil allegedly sexually assaulted her. The complaint also mentions the alleged use of a firearm to threaten her.Senior inspector Pankaj Giri of Padgha police station said six police teams had been deployed to trace the accused. Search operations were also being conducted at railway stations and airports, according to information provided by the police.Kulkarni questioned the delay in the arrests, arguing that the police act swiftly against ordinary citizens but have yet to apprehend the accused in this case. Her allegations have brought the pace of the investigation under renewed scrutiny.Meanwhile, the Bhiwandi additional sessions court had rejected Pawar's anticipatory bail application on September 28.The court observed that the allegations were serious, that a prima facie case had been made out and that custodial interrogation was necessary for an effective investigation.With both accused yet to be arrested, the focus is now on the police's efforts to trace them and the progress of the investigation amid the Congress's allegations of inaction.
Article Summary: Kanchan Kulkarni, Congress group leader in the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation (KDMC) has accused the police of inaction. She alleged that the police were extending help to the accused and demanded accountability over the delay in their arrest.

Article Title: Case against 3 from Pune for duping woman of Rs 50 lakh
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Police have booked three Pune-based businessmen for allegedly cheating a 43-year-old woman of Rs 50 lakh by promising her a partnership in a petrol pump and assuring her of monthly returns on her investment.The case was registered at Vedantnagar police station following a complaint by Shahana Ruhi Shakeel Sayyed, a resident of Rachnakar Colony.According to police, the three accused men operate a fuel station at Hadapsar, Pune.Deputy commissioner of police Pankaj Atulkar said, “The FIR is based on the documentary evidence submitted by the complainant along with her complaint.”Police said the trio allegedly convinced Sayyed to invest in the petrol pump business, claiming it was profitable and would generate regular returns.Trusting their assurances, Sayyed signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the accused on Feb 12, 2025. She later transferred Rs 50 lakh through two cheques of Rs 25 lakh each into the petrol pump’s account.According to the complaint, the accused paid returns for May and June 2025. However, they allegedly stopped making payments thereafter and failed to return her investment despite repeated demands.Claiming that she had been cheated, Sayyed approached the police with supporting documents, following which a case was registered.Police have launched an investigation into the alleged fraud. A sub-inspector-rank officer is conducting further probe.
Article Summary: The case was registered at Vedantnagar police station following a complaint by Shahana Ruhi Shakeel Sayyed, a resident of Rachnakar Colony. According to police, the three accused men operate a fuel station at Hadapsar, Pune. Police have launched an investigation into the alleged fraud.

Article Title: Two arrested for possession of MD drug worth Rs 3 lakh
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Two individuals were arrested in Kolhapur for possession of a banned mephedrone (MD) drug, worth Rs3.09 lakh and weighing around 103g, which was seized by police.Upon receiving information, police from Jaysingpur division laid a trap at Chavare village in Hatkanangle tehsil on Sunday and stopped an SUV vehicle with no number plate, in which two individuals were carrying the drug, along with 10g ganja and a pistol with four live rounds. The cops also found glassware and glass tubes that are generally used to inhale the drug in vapourised form, a pocket electronic weighing scale and lighters.The arrested individuals have been identified as Ganesh Suresh Adekar (29), a resident of Ganeshnagar, Ichalkaranji, and Sad Munir Mulla (22) from Shivajinagar, Korochi. The third accused is from Nipani in Belagavi district of Karnataka. All three have been booked under Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act and Arms Act at Peth Vadgaon police station.The police are investigating from where the drug was sourced by the accused. The cops suspect that the two arrested individuals were out to sell the MD drug. “The court has given us the custody of the accused for five days. We will dig deeper into the racket and investigate links related to the drug trade,” said Gorakh Choudhar, police inspector of Peth Vadgaon police station.
Article Summary: Two individuals were arrested in Kolhapur for possession of a banned mephedrone (MD) drug, worth Rs3.09 lakh and weighing around 103g. The arrested individuals have been identified as Ganesh Suresh Adekar (29), a resident of Ganeshnagar, Ichalkaranji, and Sad Munir Mulla (22) from Shivajinagar, Korochi.

Article Title: AICC member Khodaniya appeals Kolhapur residents to join Nov 1 Ramlila rally
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





All India Congress Committee (AICC) member and former Rajasthan minister Dinesh Khodaniya has appealed to Kolhapur residents to join the “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao” rally at New Delhi ’s Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1, to be led by leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi Addressing a news conference at the Congress office in Kolhapur, Khodaniya alleged that names of crores of voters had been deleted from electoral rolls across the country during the Election Commission of India ’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.He said Congress workers were trying to get the names of affected voters restored to the rolls and accused the BJP of weakening democracy. “We will continue our protests to demand that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar accept responsibility and resign,” Khodaniya said.Opposition parties will demand the return of ballot papers and an end to electronic voting machine use in Indian elections. “With the help of the deletions and use of EVMs, the BJP has won several elections. The people are against the BJP and it should be genuinely reflected in the voting results. Congress will keep building the heat to get reforms done in the election system,” said Khodaniya.
Article Summary: Former Rajasthan minister Dinesh Khodaniya has appealed to Kolhapur residents to join the “Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao’ rally at New Delhi ’s Ramlila Maidan on Nov 1. The rally will be led by leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: TMC suspends fire chief over immersion ghats lapses
Article Text:
Thane municipal corporation





THANE: The Thane municipal corporation (TMC) on Friday suspended its acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence in providing adequate safety equipment at idol immersion ghats on Oct 20. Action has also been taken against two other officials, while show-cause notices have been served on two junior staff, it is learnt.The suspension order is issued by additional municipal commissioner-1, Prashant Rode, holds Jhalke responsible for lapses in carrying out his duties. The order states that he has been suspended under the Maharashtra Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1979. Jhalke, who is the fire officer and in-charge of Balkum fire station, has been handling the additional charge of CFO for the last several years."Certain safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake were allegedly found to be inadequate, with a particular shortfall in life jackets and other essential safety equipment. The shortcomings were apparently pointed out to deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde who also expressed concern at the alleged negligence," said a civic official.Officials said that during the suspension period, Jhalke will be required to comply with the prescribed conditions and cannot take up other employment or engage in business without the requisite permission.
Article Summary: Thane municipal corporation suspends acting chief fire officer (CFO) over alleged negligence. Action also taken against two other officials, while show- cause notices have been served on two junior staff. Safety arrangements at Datta Mandir Ghat and Ahilyadevi Ghat at Masunda Lake allegedly found to be inadequate.

Article Title: Sealed Thane flat in Iqbal Kaskar-Dawood Ibrahim money laundering case breached; ED reclaims property, files FIR
Article Text:
Thane flat linked to Iqbal Kaskar’s extortion case targeted for occupation





MUMBAI: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane which was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim The flat was attached in the case in 2022, in the money laundering case linked to extortion by Iqbal Kaskar and others.The flat was in ED’s possession and it had put its seal on the lock. Kaskar had acquired the flat through extortion and threat in 2015 and got it registered in the name of his associate Mumtaz Azaz Sheikh, alias Raju.Recently, the ED learnt that certain persons entered the flat after removing its possession notice, claiming ownership of the flat.Since the money laundering case is pending in the court, the ED informed the court about it, repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.
Article Summary: Enforcement Directorate (ED) filed an FIR for trespassing and attempting to occupy a flat in Thane. The flat was attached in a money laundering case it investigated against Iqbal Kaskar and his Pakistan-based gangster brother Dawood Ibrahim. The ED repossessed the flat and filed a police case last week.

Article Title: Neighbour hacks elderly couple to death over cattle dispute in Purandar
Article Text:
Representative image

Pune:





A 27-year-old man allegedly hacked an elderly couple to death at Panvadi village in Purandar taluka, about 40km from Pune, on Sunday evening.The accused and the deceased were neighbours and had a dispute over the accused taking his cattle past the deceased’s house to graze. Saswad police identified the deceased as Mohan Dhiwar (83) and his wife, Ratnamala (72). The accused is on the run. The police have registered a murder case against him based on a complaint lodged by the couple’s daughter.Police inspector Santosh Gholave of Saswad police said, “The accused used to live in Pune city. About two months ago, he returned to his village. He used to graze cattle. The couple had objected a few days ago to the accused taking his cattle past their house.”The dispute had since led to frequent heated arguments between them. “On Sunday, around 5.30pm, the accused and the elderly couple again had an argument. Following this, the accused attacked them with a sharp weapon. The couple sustained severe injuries in the assault and were taken to a hospital, where doctors declared them dead. The accused fled after the incident. We have formed teams to trace him,” Gholave said.
Article Summary: A 27-year-old man allegedly hacked an elderly couple to death at Panvadi village in Purandar taluka, about 40km from Pune. The accused and the deceased were neighbours and had a dispute over the accused taking his cattle past the deceased’s house to graze. The couple sustained severe injuries in the assault and were taken to a hospital, where doctors declared them dead.

Article Title: Two arrested for firing at farmer in Nashik
Article Text:
Nashik

:





The Crime Branch Unit 1 of Nashik city police arrested two suspects in connection with a broad-daylight firing incident in Adgaon on Oct 18.A 31-year-old farmer had a narrow escape when two bike-borne men allegedly chased him and fired two rounds at him in the afternoon. Both shots missed the target, and the farmer escaped unhurt. Police registered an attempt to murder case and launched a manhunt.According to police, the prime suspect and the farmer’s wife had worked at the same company. A dispute arose between them, following which the farmer’s family asked his wife to quit the job. However, the suspect allegedly continued to harbour a grudge.The case was registered at Adgaon police station under sections 109(1) (attempt to murder) and 3(5) (criminal act by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, along with sections 3/25 of the Arms Act.Acting on a tip-off received by police personnel Pravin Waghmare and Vishal Devare, a police team intercepted and arrested Rahul Ambekar (35) and Vikas Waluba Sonawane (25) near Kushire Mala on Ramwadi Road in Nashik.
Article Summary: A 31-year-old farmer had a narrow escape when two bike-borne men allegedly chased him and fired two rounds at him in the afternoon. Police registered an attempt to murder case and launched a manhunt. Rahul Ambekar (35) and Vikas Waluba Sonawane (25) were arrested.

Article Title: Granting anticipatory bail to Anbil Mahesh will paralyse probe: HC
Article Text:
anbil mahesh

Chennai:





“While protection of individual liberty is a duty of the court, it should be weighed against society’s need for a corruption-free govt administration,” Madras high court said while refusing anticipatory bail to former school education minister Anbil Mahesh on Monday.“This court is of the view that if anticipatory bail is granted in this case, it would paralyse the investigation. The records show that 177 victims have so far come forward to record their statements,” said Justice V Lakshminarayanan.The ex-minister had apprehended arrest in connection with the ₹100 crore private schools recognition cheating case.“The petitioner is a politician holding a high position. If AB is granted before the A2 ( Muthukumar , a former DMK MLA who is absconding) is apprehended, then it would become a tool for Muthukumar to avoid the process of the investigation,” the court added. “Also, prima facie, the records reveal that the absconding accused (A2 has been shielded by the petitioner,” it said.“... Anbil Mahesh faces accusations of having received monies under the name and style of the party fund. As to who is the final destination of this alleged party fund cannot be unearthed unless and until the petitioner is interrogated,” the judge said.Dismissing the contention of senior advocate P Wilson, who represented Anbil Mahesh, that the probe ought to be done only by DVAC, as it is the specialised force in matters of corruption, the judge said, “I am not in a position to agree with the submission, for a simple reason that there is a division of work in the police force among its several departments.““It is not as if DVAC alone possesses the exclusive jurisdiction to investigate matters relating to corruption,” the court said. “As to who should investigate is a matter which is exclusively within the jurisdiction of the police. Unless and until there is an inherent lack of jurisdiction, this court will not interfere as to who takes up the matter for investigation.”
Article Summary: Madras high court refuses anticipatory bail to former school education minister Anbil Mahesh. Ex-minister had apprehended arrest in connection with the ₹100 crore private schools recognition cheating case. 177 victims have so far come forward to record their statements.

Article Title: DMK, Congress, Left parties walk demanding CEC’s resignation
Article Text:
File photo

TOI





Chennai: Demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, major parties including DMK CPI and CPM walked out of the all-party meeting on special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls at Ripon Buildings here on Monday.This comes days after members of TVK, DMK, Congress, and other parties walked out of the all-party meeting on SSR in the secretariat on Oct 23, making similar demand.The meeting on Monday, chaired by the district election officer and Greater Chennai Corporation commissioner G S Sameeran, was to discuss the SSR of electoral rolls, with Jan 1, 2027 as the qualifying date, and changes to polling station arrangements across the district’s 16 assembly constituencies. The number of polling stations has been reduced from 4,079 to 4,071. This reduced one in Dr Radhakrishnan Nagar, merged five polling stations in Chepauk-Triplicane, two in Thousand Lights and two in Mylapore constituency.Before the meeting formally began, DMK and Congress members walked out once the commissioner entered the hall, said SK Siva, district secretary for South Chennai, Communist Party of India. “Once the commissioner announced what the meeting was convened for, I and CPM members said that Gyanesh Kumar must resign and until then we will not participate in any meetings related to SIR,” he said, adding that no action has been taken against the CEC for the alleged irregularities in SIR.More than 97 lakh votes in Tamil Nadu and 14 lakh votes in Chennai were deleted, as per data released by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in Dec 2025.DMK deputy general secretary and MP Kanimozhi toldthat the party had made several attempts to state its stand on the issue. “We have clearly said that Gyanesh Kumar must resign. The walkout mirrors the same effort. We are soon going to meet the President and raise the issue,” she said.
Article Summary: Major parties including DMK CPI and CPM walked out of the all-party meeting on special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls at Ripon Buildings here on Monday. This comes days after members of TVK, DMK, Congress, and other parties walk out of an all- party meeting on SSR in the secretariat.

Article Title: Even before Dhanush announces his political entry, AIADMK backs the actor, while TVK and Congress call it BJP’s plan
Article Text:

Actor Dhanush is yet to announce his political plans. But speculation about his political entry has triggered opposition from TVK and Congress , who allege that the actor’s moves were part of a BJP -backed strategy to counter chief minister C Joseph Vijay . Article Summary: TVK and Congress allege that the actor’s moves were part of a BJP -backed strategy to counter chief minister C Joseph Vijay. BJP, however, has distanced itself from the actor, even as its ally AIADMK backed Dhanush.

Article Title: Man held for murdering homosexual partner in Tirupur
Article Text:
Tirupur

:





A textile worker was arrested for murdering his homosexual partner by hitting him on the head with a grinding stone at a rented room in Chamundipuram on Saturday.Police said the deceased Muthu , 26, and the accused Chinnaram, 21, both from Madurai district, were working at a private knitwear unit and living together on the terrace of an apartment building near Chamundipuram.The crime came to light on Sunday, when neighbours found Muthu dead inside the room. 15 Velampalayam police who were alerted, recovered the body and sent it to Tirupur Govt Hospital for a postmortem.Police launched a search for Chinnaram, who was missing from the room. Meanwhile, Chinnaram surrendered at Usilampatti police station in Madurai district on Sunday, after which a Tirupur police team secured him and brought him to Tirupur for interrogation.“During questioning, he revealed that the two had been living together for about six years. An argument broke out on Saturday night after Muthu’s family began looking for a bride for him. Chinnaram objected to the marriage plans, and the quarrel escalated, following which he allegedly used a grinding stone to assault Muthu, killing him,” said a police officer.Meanwhile, police also scotched rumours that the murder was linked to alleged threats involving a video. “No such video was found on either of their mobile phones,” the officer added.A case has been registered and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A textile worker was arrested for murdering his homosexual partner by hitting him on the head with a grinding stone at a rented room in Chamundipuram. Police said the deceased Muthu, 26, and the accused Chinnaram, 21, both from Madurai district, were working at a private knitwear unit and living together.

Article Title: 864 bottles of liquor seized from house near Erode; man arrested
Article Text: ERODE: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district in the early hours of Thursday and arrested a man.Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid at the house of K Govindaraj, 28, of Ammapalayam. They found 864 bottles of IMFL stocked in the house for illegal sale.Police registered a case and arrested Govindaraj. He was remanded in judicial custody.They launched a search for Sekar alias Ammasai, 34, and Sridhar, 38, who have links with the illegal liquor operation.
Article Summary: Police seized 864 bottles of Indian made foreign liquor (IMFL) from a house near Mylambadi in Erode district. Acting on a tip-off that bottles of liquor had been illegally stored for unauthorised sale, the Bhavani police conducted a raid.

Article Title: Man held for sexual assault bid on blind woman on moving train
Article Text:
Kasaragod

:





Railway police arrested a 24-year-old man for allegedly attempting to sexually assault a blind woman on a moving train in Kasaragod on Sunday. The arrested person is Ayyappa from Karnataka The survivor, 49, was travelling in the coach reserved for specially-abled persons of a special train bound for Lokmanya Tilak Terminus in Mumbai. She was returning home along with her nine-year-old son after attending a meeting in Ernakulam.When the train passed Kozhikode, only the woman and her son remained in the coach. The accused boarded the train from Kannur and attacked her when the train reached Payyannur, police said. He pushed her off her seat and tightly choked her around the face and neck. In an attempt to escape from him, she asked her son to pull the emergency chain to stop the train, police said.When the train stopped, the accused jumped off and boarded a nearby coach. The railway staff intimated the incident to Kasaragod railway police. The police reached the spot and arrested the accused with support from other passengers.The woman, who suffered injuries on the face and neck during the scuffle, was admitted to a hospital.
Article Summary: Woman, 49, was travelling in the coach reserved for specially-abled persons of a special train bound for Lokmanya Tilak Terminus in Mumbai. She was returning home along with her nine-year-old son after attending a meeting in Ernakulam. The accused pushed her off her seat and tightly choked her around the face and neck.

Article Title: Christian trust seeks to implead in plea challenging Kerala waqf board reconstitution
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Assembly of Christian Trust Services (ACTS), a public religious charitable trust based in Thiruvananthapuram , has filed an interlocutory application seeking to implead itself in a petition filed by former state waqf board chairman K M Hamza and others challenging the govt order reconstituting the board.ACTS stated that a PIL filed by it challenging the board’s reconstitution in Feb 2026 without including non-Muslim members, as required under the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, is still pending before the division bench. Meanwhile, the state govt reconstituted the board through another order dated Oct 16, which is now under challenge by Hamza and others. ACTS contended that its impleadment was necessary to avoid conflicting decisions and multiplicity of proceedings. It sought a directive to make it a party to the pending petition.The impleading application also stated that most non-Muslim MPs from the ruling parties and members of the bar council were unwilling to serve on the board. Accordingly, ACTS proposed the names of certain non-Muslim MPs, including Suresh Gopi , K Radhakrishnan and K Francis George, as well as certain non-Muslim members of the bar council, for consideration for the respective positions.
Article Summary: Assembly of Christian Trust Services (ACTS), a public religious charitable trust based in Thiruvananthapuram, has filed an interlocutory application seeking to implead itself in a petition filed by former state waqf board chairman K M Hamza. ACTS contended that its impleadment was necessary to avoid conflicting decisions and multiplicity of proceedings.

Article Title: Writer levels plagiarism charge against Vayalar Award winner
Article Text:
Kottayam

:





Writer Vinayasree on Monday said the plagiarism allegation against the novel that won this year’s Vayalar Award should be examined, and that the award should be reconsidered.Addressing a news conference in Alappuzha, she said the allegation is that ideas and dialogue moments from her earlier works, Panchaliyude Ezhurathrikal, Hidimbi and Shikhandi, had been reproduced almost exactly in the award-winning work. All three of her books are based on characters and plots from the Mahabharata.She said writers are free to write on mythological epics. However, a literary examination is warranted when character portrayals, the conception of dialogues and the narrative treatment of events appear similar in another work, she said.She said the award should not have been granted without an independent examination of the allegations and of the novel’s originality. She has submitted a complaint to the chief minister, the culture minister and the Vayalar Award selection committee seeking this, she added.A defamation case is pending against Vinayasree at the Thalassery munsiff court over a Facebook post she made in 2025. The plaintiff is seeking Rs 5 lakh in compensation.
Article Summary: Writer Vinayasree says plagiarism allegation against the novel that won this year’s Vayalar Award should be examined. She said ideas and dialogue moments from her earlier works had been reproduced almost exactly in the award-winning work. All three of her books are based on characters and plots from the Mahabharata.
